title: Multiplying Fractions — visual

body.title: Multiplying Fractions — visual

visual.caption: Longer shaded bar = larger fraction when the whole is the same.

body.explanation: Use the picture to understand multiplying fractions. Example: Calculate 1/2 × 1/3. → 1/6. Multiply numerators and denominators: 1×1 / 2×3.
body.misconception_check: The picture shows why this is wrong: Multiplies fractions by adding instead

prompt:
You are a Year 5 maths tutor. Teach using VISUAL EXPLANATION (fraction bars / number lines).

Skill: multiplying fractions
Active misconception to address: Multiplies fractions by adding instead
Teaching method: visual

Rules:
- Describe fraction bars or a number line in plain text (ASCII is fine).
- Make the visual do the teaching; keep words short.
- Explicitly show why this misconception is wrong: Multiplies fractions by adding instead
- Then give 3 practice questions.
- You MUST use these exact correct answers:
- example mul_01: 1/6
- mul_02: 1/5
- mul_03: 1/2
- mul_04: 1/6

Return JSON only with this shape:
{
  "title": "...",
  "method": "visual",
  "visual": {"type": "fraction_bars|number_line", "ascii": "...", "caption": "..."},
  "explanation": "2-4 short sentences",
  "misconception_check": "one sentence correcting the misconception",
  "practice": [{"id": "...", "prompt": "...", "answer": "..."}],
  "exit_ticket": {"prompt": "...", "answer": "..."}
}

Practice stems (use these; keep their answers exactly):
- id=mul_02 | Calculate 2/5 × 1/2. | CORRECT_ANSWER=1/5
- id=mul_03 | Calculate 3/4 × 2/3. | CORRECT_ANSWER=1/2
- id=mul_04 | What is 1/4 of 2/3? (Same as 1/4 × 2/3.) | CORRECT_ANSWER=1/6
